rationale: C06 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both proclamations redefine an existing national monument through a comprehensive metes-and-bounds description, declare that the newly described tract shall constitute the monument, amend the original establishing proclamation, revoke an earlier federal reservation as to included lands, and conclude with nearly identical monument-protection warnings. This combination and sequence are more distinctive than the generic monument-enlargement formula. C22 is also strong because it adds formerly military-reserved land, revokes the military withdrawal, and uses closely parallel warning language. C16 shares the interdepartmental-transfer predicate and application of monument laws, but its operative structure is less closely aligned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the following-described tract of land, which comprises the original site of the monument and the additional lands needed for the purposes stated above, shall constitute the Cabrillo National Monument
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the lands now owned by the United States within the exterior boundaries of the following-described tracts of land ... shall constitute the Sitka National Monument
shared_material.explanation: Both redefine the entire monument through a newly stated exterior-boundary description rather than merely listing an isolated addition.

shared_material.child_excerpt: [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] establishing the Cabrillo National Monument is amended accordingly. The withdrawal order of February 26, 1852, is hereby revoked as to the lands described above.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The said [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 23, 1910, is amended accordingly. [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of August 16, 1941 ... is hereby revoked as to the lands comprising the said Tract No. 2
shared_material.explanation: The same paired administrative machinery follows the land description: amendment of the founding proclamation and partial revocation of a prior federal reservation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, deface, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands reserved by this proclamation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.
shared_material.explanation: The protective warning is nearly verbatim, although this clause alone would be boilerplate; it reinforces the more distinctive shared operative sequence.
